network.overall_strategy: Use a plausible hydrothermal C4 precursor, succinic acid, rather than force a poorly constrained C1/C2 build. H2-driven Fe-Ni reduction gives succinaldehyde, which enters nitrogen chemistry by direct reductive amination or by cyclizing reductive amination to 1-pyrroline, an explicit reservoir for the unstable 4-aminobutanal/1-pyrroline pair. A single main hydrothermal-to-surface transfer is then used because HCN capture and low-water cyanamide chemistry are better supported in cooler surface films. Surface Strecker chemistry gives ornithine nitrile, after which the network branches into ornithine-first and nitrile-first finishes: ornithine nitrile can be hydrolyzed in acidic pools or silica wet-dry films, then guanidinated with cyanamide or dicyandiamide; alternatively it can be guanidinated before hydrolysis to exploit reduced alpha-amine nucleophilicity. The main bottlenecks are the initial succinate-to-succinaldehyde reduction and late-stage side-chain-selective guanidination. All aminonitrile hydrolyses are intended as net two-water additions with ammonia release; coefficients are implicit in the schema.

reactions.name: Hydrothermal reduction of succinic acid to succinaldehyde

conditions.other: Subseafloor H2-rich alkaline vent pores; net stoichiometry is succinic acid + 2 H2 -> succinaldehyde + 2 H2O

reactions.mechanism: Adsorbed carboxylates undergo H2-driven reduction on Fe-Ni sulfides and alloys, plausibly via transient surface acyl or formyl intermediates, to give the dialdehyde.
reactions.reasoning: Reduced C4 dicarboxylates are more plausible vent organics than free dialdehydes. The dialdehyde-forming reduction is speculative, but H2-rich Fe-Ni sulfide and alloy systems are among the few prebiotic settings capable of supplying both the needed reducing power and surface activation.

reactions.name: Direct mineral-catalyzed reductive amination of succinaldehyde

conditions.other: NH3-rich vent mixing zone; short residence times help limit overreduction and diamination

reactions.mechanism: One aldehyde forms an imine with ammonia and is reduced by surface-activated H2, leaving the second aldehyde intact.
reactions.reasoning: Direct mono-reductive amination gives the shortest route to 4-aminobutanal, but the step competes with cyclization to 1-pyrroline and possible overreduction. It is therefore included as a plausible branch rather than assumed to dominate.

reactions.name: Cyclizing reductive amination of succinaldehyde to 1-pyrroline

conditions.other: NH3-rich vent mixing zone; net stoichiometry is succinaldehyde + NH3 + H2 -> 1-pyrroline + 2 H2O

reactions.mechanism: One aldehyde is reductively aminated; the resulting aminoaldehyde then cyclizes onto the second aldehyde and dehydrates to the cyclic imine.
reactions.reasoning: Cyclization is intrinsically favored once an aminoaldehyde is generated, so explicit inclusion of 1-pyrroline captures the expected speciation better than treating 4-aminobutanal as permanently open-chain. This branch likely represents a realistic reservoir during transport into cooler surface waters.

reactions.name: Hydrolytic ring opening of 1-pyrroline to 4-aminobutanal

conditions.other: Vent-discharge margin or prebiotic pool; reversible ring-opening equilibrium during cooling and dilution

reactions.mechanism: Imine hydration followed by ring opening regenerates the open-chain aminoaldehyde.
reactions.reasoning: 1-Pyrroline and 4-aminobutanal are in reversible aqueous equilibrium. The ring-opened form need not accumulate strongly; it only has to be regenerated often enough for cyanide trapping in the next step.

reactions.name: Strecker capture of 4-aminobutanal to ornithine nitrile

conditions.other: Evaporitic pool or tidal-film concentration of HCN and NH3; rapid trapping of open-chain aminoaldehyde required

reactions.mechanism: Strecker addition: aldehyde imination with ammonia followed by cyanide capture gives the alpha-aminonitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Strecker capture is the most chemically direct way to convert the remaining aldehyde into the alpha-amino acid skeleton. High NH3 and HCN concentration and cooling are important because 4-aminobutanal is short-lived and otherwise re-cyclizes.

reactions.name: Acidic pool hydrolysis of ornithine nitrile to ornithine

conditions.other: Acidic volcanic hot-spring pool or sulfate-rich film; net stoichiometry is ornithine nitrile + 2 H2O -> ornithine + NH3

reactions.mechanism: Sequential nitrile hydration to amide and then carboxylic acid with ammonia release.
reactions.reasoning: Acidic wet-heating is the more defensible nitrile-to-amino-acid hydrolysis mode here. This step explicitly represents the net transformation aminonitrile + 2 H2O -> amino acid + NH3, avoiding the under-specified hydrolyses that weakened earlier networks.

reactions.name: Silica-film wet-dry hydrolysis of ornithine nitrile to ornithine

conditions.other: Silica-sinter wet-dry cycling in a subaerial geothermal field; net stoichiometry is ornithine nitrile + 2 H2O -> ornithine + NH3

reactions.mechanism: Progressive nitrile hydration occurs over repeated wetting and concentration cycles on silica films.
reactions.reasoning: Silica-rich wet-dry films offer a second, more environmentally continuous surface hydrolysis route after Strecker capture. This branch is probably slower than rxn_006 but gentler and better aligned with repeated concentration and rehydration cycles.

reactions.name: Dry-state cyanamide guanidination of ornithine

conditions.other: Low-water geothermal film, mildly basic; repeated drying suppresses cyanamide hydrolysis

reactions.mechanism: Terminal amine addition to cyanamide followed by proton transfer and tautomerization furnishes the guanidino group.
reactions.reasoning: Cyanamide is a credible prebiotic amidinyl source under low-water conditions. Direct guanidination of ornithine is chemically plausible on mineral films, but side-chain versus alpha-amine selectivity remains a genuine uncertainty, so this branch is retained as one option rather than the sole finish.

reactions.name: Dry-state dimerization of cyanamide to dicyandiamide

conditions.other: Dry-down on evaporitic or geothermal crust; net stoichiometry is 2 cyanamide -> dicyandiamide

reactions.mechanism: Thermal condensation of two cyanamide molecules to N-cyanoguanidine.
reactions.reasoning: Warm dry surfaces naturally convert part of a cyanamide inventory into dicyandiamide. Including this reaction captures a realistic surface-aging process and provides an alternative amidino donor without requiring a wholly different feedstock class.

reactions.name: Dicyandiamide-mediated guanidination of ornithine

conditions.other: Low-water reheating of dicyandiamide-rich film; released cyanamide can recycle

reactions.mechanism: Amidino transfer from dicyandiamide to the terminal amine expels cyanamide.
reactions.reasoning: Dicyandiamide is less labile than cyanamide and can act as a buffered amidino donor in reheated low-water films. The step is slower than direct cyanamide addition and still faces regioselectivity challenges, but it gives a chemically distinct surface route to arginine.

reactions.name: Dry-state cyanamide guanidination of ornithine nitrile

conditions.other: Drying silica film with limited water activity; nitrile is retained during amidination

reactions.mechanism: The side-chain amine adds to cyanamide and tautomerizes to the amidino product while the aminonitrile remains intact.
reactions.reasoning: Guanidination before nitrile hydrolysis may improve selectivity because the alpha-amino group of an aminonitrile is electronically damped by the adjacent nitrile, leaving the terminal side-chain amine relatively more nucleophilic. This is one of the stronger late-stage branches in the network.

reactions.name: Acidic hydrolysis of arginine nitrile to arginine

conditions.other: Acidic hot-spring rehydration after dry-down; net stoichiometry is arginine nitrile + 2 H2O -> arginine + NH3

reactions.mechanism: Stepwise nitrile hydration and hydrolysis convert the nitrile to the carboxylic acid.
reactions.reasoning: Once the guanidino group is installed, ordinary aminonitrile hydrolysis completes the amino acid. Moderate acidic surface rehydration is preferred because the guanidino group is robust enough to survive it, whereas prolonged hotter conditions risk broader decomposition.

pathways.name: Direct aminoaldehyde / acidic hydrolysis / cyanamide
pathways.description: Shortest ornithine-first route: direct hydrothermal aminoaldehyde formation, surface Strecker capture, acidic hydrolysis to ornithine, then cyanamide guanidination.

pathways.name: Direct aminoaldehyde / acidic hydrolysis / dicyandiamide
pathways.description: Branched ornithine-first route: direct aminoaldehyde formation and Strecker capture are followed by a parallel surface dry-down that converts cyanamide to dicyandiamide before final amidino transfer to ornithine.

pathways.name: Direct aminoaldehyde / silica hydrolysis / cyanamide
pathways.description: Direct aminoaldehyde branch with silica-sinter wet-dry hydrolysis instead of bulk acidic hydrolysis before cyanamide guanidination.

pathways.name: Direct aminoaldehyde / silica hydrolysis / dicyandiamide
pathways.description: Direct aminoaldehyde branch plus silica-film hydrolysis and a parallel dicyandiamide-generating dry-down before the final amidino transfer.

pathways.name: Pyrroline reservoir / acidic hydrolysis / cyanamide
pathways.description: Cyclization-prone C4 chemistry is routed through a 1-pyrroline reservoir, reopened in surface water, then hydrolyzed in acidic pools before cyanamide guanidination.

pathways.name: Pyrroline reservoir / acidic hydrolysis / dicyandiamide
pathways.description: Pyrroline reservoir route with acidic hydrolysis, plus a parallel cyanamide dry-down that supplies dicyandiamide for the final amidino transfer.

pathways.name: Pyrroline reservoir / silica hydrolysis / cyanamide
pathways.description: Pyrroline reservoir route with silica-sinter hydrolysis of ornithine nitrile and direct cyanamide finish.

pathways.name: Pyrroline reservoir / silica hydrolysis / dicyandiamide
pathways.description: Pyrroline reservoir route with silica-film hydrolysis and a parallel dicyandiamide-mediated finish.

pathways.name: Direct aminoaldehyde / nitrile-first guanidination
pathways.description: Direct aminoaldehyde branch followed by Strecker capture, guanidination at the aminonitrile stage, then hydrolysis to arginine.

pathways.name: Pyrroline reservoir / nitrile-first guanidination
pathways.description: Reservoir-controlled version of the nitrile-first finish, using 1-pyrroline as the carrier of the unstable aminoaldehyde before Strecker capture and late hydrolysis.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Formally reaches arginine, but confidence is capped by rxn_001 and rxn_002: direct hydrothermal reduction of free succinic acid to succinaldehyde is weakly supported, and 4-aminobutyraldehyde is unstable and difficult to transfer or use as a discrete intermediate. Acidic aminonitrile hydrolysis is reasonable, but cyanamide guanidination of free ornithine remains selectivity-limited.
suggestions: Provide stronger support or an activation step for rxn_001 rather than direct reduction of the free diacid.
Use the 1-pyrroline reservoir route to avoid handling free 4-aminobutyraldehyde across environments.
Add a concrete selectivity rationale favoring side-chain guanidination over alpha-guanidination.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Dicyandiamide formation is plausible, but this variant keeps the same two early bottlenecks and still relies on selective guanidination of free ornithine in rxn_010. The extra dry-state step does not clearly improve the overall route.
suggestions: Show that dicyandiamide materially improves side-chain guanidination selectivity relative to cyanamide.
Strengthen or replace rxn_001 with a more experimentally supported reduction or activation sequence.
Specify dry-state conditions that allow guanidination without extensive decomposition of ornithine.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Silica wet-dry films may help concentration, but nitrile hydrolysis is less directly supported there than in an acidic pool, so this direct-aminoaldehyde variant is weaker than P1. The route still inherits the unstable free-aminoaldehyde transfer and late guanidination selectivity problems.
suggestions: Provide evidence that silica wet-dry films can hydrolyze ornithine nitrile efficiently under the stated conditions.
Avoid transfer of free 4-aminobutyraldehyde by routing through 1-pyrroline.
Clarify how low-water cyanamide chemistry favors side-chain over alpha-guanidination.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This route combines the less secure silica-film nitrile hydrolysis with the less selective dicyandiamide guanidination of free ornithine. It remains dominated by the same weak early chemistry in rxn_001 and rxn_002.
suggestions: Support silica-assisted nitrile hydrolysis with experimental precedent under wet-dry cycling.
Demonstrate that dicyandiamide improves side-chain selectivity enough to justify the extra step.
Replace the free-aminoaldehyde transfer with the 1-pyrroline reservoir branch.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Using 1-pyrroline as a reservoir is more chemically coherent than moving free 4-aminobutyraldehyde between environments. The pathway is still limited by the low-confidence succinate reduction and by guanidination of free ornithine.
suggestions: Strengthen rxn_001 or insert an activation step before carboxyl reduction.
Specify catalyst and H2 conditions that favor 1-pyrroline over over-reduced products.
Consider the nitrile-first finish to reduce guanidination selectivity problems.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The 1-pyrroline reservoir improves stability and transfer, but dicyandiamide adds a step without clearly solving the selectivity problem at the ornithine stage. Early confidence is still limited by rxn_001.
suggestions: Demonstrate that dicyandiamide improves side-chain selectivity enough to justify the extra step.
Specify conditions that stop rxn_003 at 1-pyrroline rather than pyrrolidine or other reduced products.
Consider shifting guanidination to the aminonitrile stage.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Reservoir logic is good, but silica-film hydrolysis is less secure than acidic hydrolysis and the late ornithine guanidination is still weak. This is a coherent route, just not a high-confidence one.
suggestions: Support silica-assisted nitrile hydrolysis with experimental precedent under wet-dry cycling.
Specify conditions that favor 1-pyrroline formation and preservation.
Prefer nitrile-first guanidination if selectivity is the main concern.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This route benefits from the 1-pyrroline reservoir, but the silica-film hydrolysis and dicyandiamide guanidination steps both reduce confidence relative to the best branches. The network still depends on the weak early reduction in rxn_001.
suggestions: Provide direct support for silica-film hydrolysis of ornithine nitrile under the stated wet-dry conditions.
Show that dicyandiamide offers a real selectivity gain over cyanamide on this substrate set.
Constrain rxn_003 to the cyclic imine endpoint rather than more reduced products.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Among the direct-aminoaldehyde routes, this is the strongest because nitrile-first guanidination should suppress some alpha-amine competition. The main remaining weaknesses are rxn_001 and the need to generate and trap 4-aminobutyraldehyde quickly before cyclization or side reactions.
suggestions: Demonstrate rapid surface Strecker capture from the 4-aminobutyraldehyde and 1-pyrroline equilibrium.
Provide evidence that ornithine nitrile guanidination is mainly side-chain selective.
Strengthen or replace rxn_001 with a more supported reduction or activation step.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Best route overall. 1-pyrroline provides a realistic reservoir and transfer form for the unstable aminoaldehyde, and nitrile-first guanidination is the most credible late-stage selectivity strategy. Confidence is still capped by rxn_001 and by uncertain endpoint control in rxn_003 under H2-rich hydrothermal conditions.
suggestions: Provide stronger support or an activation step for rxn_001, which is the main network bottleneck.
Specify hydrothermal catalyst and temperature windows that stop rxn_003 at 1-pyrroline rather than more reduced products.
Validate that ornithine nitrile guanidination followed by acidic hydrolysis preserves the guanidino group and gives the target regioisomer.

evaluation.network_feedback: Graph-level validity is strong: the network is connected, molecule IDs are consistent, and the RDKit check reports 0 unbalanced reactions. Stoichiometric coefficients should still be made explicit for rxn_001 (2 H2 and 2 H2O), rxn_003 (2 H2O), rxn_006 and rxn_007 plus rxn_012 (2 H2O with NH3 release), and rxn_009 (2 cyanamide), but these are not conservation failures. Environmental partitioning is generally sensible, especially hydrothermal H2/Fe-Ni chemistry followed by cooler surface HCN and cyanamide chemistry. Confidence is limited mainly by chemistry: rxn_001 is a weakly supported reduction of free succinic acid to succinaldehyde, rxn_002 and rxn_003 need tighter endpoint control, and free-ornithine guanidination is poorly selective. The strongest branch is P10 because it uses 1-pyrroline as a realistic reservoir for the 4-aminobutyraldehyde pair and delays guanidination until the aminonitrile stage. Overall, this is a coherent but not approval-level network that needs stronger experimental support at the early reduction and late selectivity bottlenecks.
